document_title: The Every-day Life of Abraham Lincoln: A Narrative And Descriptive Biography With Pen-Pictures And Personal; Recollections By Those Who Knew Him
author: Francis F. Browne
claims: Abraham Lincoln was at the War Department with a small group to hear election returns.
General Eckert brought telegrams with election returns to the War Department.
Mr. Stanton read the election returns, and President Lincoln commented on them.
During a lull in the returns, Lincoln read from a pamphlet by Petroleum V. Nasby to Charles A. Dana.
Mr. Stanton appeared impatient with Lincoln's reading of the pamphlet.
Lincoln received news of his nomination for President.
A messenger from the telegraph office delivered a dispatch announcing the nomination.
The dispatch stated that Mr. Seward was the second man on the list.
A cheer was proposed for Abraham Lincoln as the next President.
Lincoln read the dispatch aloud after reading it in silence.
Lincoln remarked that a 'little woman' would be interested in the news and he would go home to tell her.
A salute of a hundred guns was fired in Springfield when the news spread.
Lincoln's friends and neighbors visited his house to offer congratulations.
An enthusiastic meeting was held by Republicans at the State House in the evening.
Republicans marched to the Lincoln mansion after the meeting.
Lincoln appeared and gave a brief, modest, and hearty speech.
Lincoln invited attendees into his house.
The crowd responded that they would give him a larger house after March 4th.
